goal: Rill West and Rill East were monitored during the same two-hour diversion trial. Did West deliver more water than East during the part of the trial measured on both channels, and is that ordering robust to the stated calibration bounds? Give the valid comparison duration, both volumes and the signed excess interval. Which channel, if either, deserves a follow-up check? Explain how missing observations constrain any statement about the entire trial.

operation.reason: The calculated West-minus-East excess is positive throughout the stated calibration interval for the jointly observed part of the supplied synthetic trial. Check West first to verify its higher delivery against the intended diversion setting.
unresolved: East lacks a valid rate in the earlier gap and West lacks one in the later gap. Each rejected rate has no usable bound, so either channel could have delivered more over the full trial.
The cause of the difference during shared coverage is unknown.

final_decision.rationale: The paired integration answers the delivery question for the shared valid time. West still leads when all its rates take their lower calibration limits and East's take their upper limits. That makes West the first channel to check. A second calculation on the same record would add no information about the rejected rates or the cause of the imbalance.
